name: Julian Antecessor
bio: Julian Antecessor is one of the named epigrammatists whose short poems are preserved in the Greek Anthology. Paton's Index of Authors dates the poet to the 6th century AD (?).
This archive carries the 3 epigrams ascribed to the poet in the fourth volume of W. R. Paton's prose translation (Loeb, 1918): Book XI: 367, 368, 369.

poems.title: Book XI, 367
poems.author: Julian Antecessor
poems.text: You have a face just like an ostrich. Did Circe give you a potion to drink and change your nature into that of a bird ?

poems.title: Book XI, 368
poems.author: Julian Antecessor
poems.text: You have sucha heavy crop on your hairy face that you ought to have it cut with scythes and not with scissors.

poems.title: Book XI, 369
poems.author: Julian Antecessor
poems.text: Live in safety in the town, lest the stork who delights in the blood of Pygmies peck you.
